### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-openapi`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in replacement))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2e0dbfd9177f80b43ec703655ef967f9972c220d` — the merge of head `188a8286353413c982a115f6f5831e08322bb9ff` into base `020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2e0dbfd9177f80b43ec703655ef967f9972c220d && git checkout 2e0dbfd9177f80b43ec703655ef967f9972c220d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70 188a8286353413c982a115f6f5831e08322bb9ff && git checkout -B drift-repro 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70 && git merge --no-ff 188a8286353413c982a115f6f5831e08322bb9ff

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 020ce3d9e8c7ac9a97863cf31e151290d4938a70` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cxHwXNcGcAHNerZsom

Request: review · area A5 · head 10a4106a1825444edb72e84a9c9c299ebf60082b · contract

Fixes #33553. A `connector_action` node refuses, before dispatch, any input key the chosen action's input schema does not declare (top level and inside sections, on the evaluated input). The step fails with `VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the node, the key's dotted path and the declared keys; nothing is sent; a fault edge can catch it. A schema that admits more keys (additionalProperties true/schema, patternProperties, composition, `$ref`, no properties) stays open. The check is opt-in on the shared `judgeConnectorInput`, so the connector pull door is unchanged (pinned). Publish-time refusal is not built: measured that at boot the flow pull registers flows before connectors materialize, so a registration verdict would be a startup-order defect; reason in the PR body. Clause-② yes (narrowing), Metadata-protocol narrowed, ADR-0087 semantic entry `connector-action-undeclared-input-key-refused` added (one spec file, surface widened by A5). +~270 lines, service-automation minor. First-party producers (DocuSign, Stripe, showcase Slack/REST/MCP) send only declared keys. Out-of-scope: connector pull `connectorSource.input` has the same gap (Acceptance notes).

Posted 2026-11-15T03:24Z.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `10a4106a1825444edb72e84a9c9c299ebf60082b`
Local-runs: probe — ran this head's `connector-input-schema.ts` alone (node strip-types, no build) against the schema shape connector-openapi emits when it skips a `$ref` parameter or request body, to confirm the M1 refusal
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-action-undeclared-input-key-refused.ts + .changeset/33553-connector-action-undeclared-input-key.md, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-input-schema.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-input-schema.test.ts; read only: packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/scripts/normalize-openapi.mts, packages/connectors/connector-slack/src/slack-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-rest/src/rest-connector.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, packages/services/service-automation/CHANGELOG.md (the #27995 / #28040 entries)

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A5 · Fixes #33553 (p2) · narrowing face plus one spec path. Read-only: the diff, the head tree, the cited producers, the issue, and the head's check runs, including the Check Changeset job log. One local probe, named above.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Where the refusal happens.** The refusal sits in the `connector_action` executor (connector-nodes.ts ~149-180). It runs after `resolveValueSlotMap`, so it judges the EVALUATED input, and before `handler(input, ...)`, so nothing is sent. It returns `success: false, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, the same runtime failure #27995 uses, so a `fault` edge receives it (test 6.1 asserts this). The message names the node, each `'dotted.path'` and the keys declared at that level. `UNDECLARED_KEY_HINT` is appended only when `undeclaredKey` is set.
- **How the walk finds keys.** The undeclared-key loop runs inside the `kind === 'object'` branch of `collectInputSchemaViolations`, after the walk has descended into `properties`. So a section is judged against its own sub-schema (`query.stale`, test 6.4), and so is an object inside an array's `items` (see N1). A type mismatch returns early, so a value of the wrong type is not also reported key by key. An `undefined` value is skipped and `null` is refused (test 6.2), which matches what reaches the wire.
- **Which schemas are open.** `declaredKeysOf` returns `undefined` (open) for any key-admitting keyword in `KEY_ADMITTING_KEYWORDS`, for `additionalProperties` or `unevaluatedProperties` set to anything but `false`, and for a schema with no `properties` that is not `additionalProperties: false`. Otherwise it returns `properties` ∪ `required`. Five open shapes are pinned as still dispatching (test 6.6). Ablation leg 2 in the PR body reds that case; I read this as the author's report and did not re-run it.
- **The pull door is unchanged.** `connector-pull.ts` is not in the diff. The option defaults to off (`options.refuseUndeclaredKeys === true`). The pin (test 6.8) is at the judge level (see N4).
- **Boot order, verified on this head.** In `plugin.ts` `start()`, the flow pull calls `registerFlow` (~2567-2590) before `materializeDeclaredConnectors(ctx, { fatal: true })` (~2676). Stored connector entries wait for `kernel:bootstrapped` (~2689). So at registration the action schemas of declarative connectors are not yet known, as the PR body measured.
- **The producer gap (M1).** connector-openapi's `buildInputSchema` (openapi-connector.ts ~512-552) `continue`s past a `$ref` parameter. `extractRequestBodySchema` returns `undefined` for a `$ref` request body and for content with no `schema`. The emitted schema then lists only the remaining sections. The declarative `openapi` provider does not dereference: a URL or file spec is `JSON.parse`d and checked to be 3.x (openapi-provider.ts ~150-225). `normalize-openapi.mts` is an offline, optional step. connectors.mdx refuses only Swagger 2.0 and describes the normalizer as the step "the repository carries", not as required for 3.x. The handler still sends what the schema dropped: `interpolatePath`, `serializeQuery` and `serializeHeaders` fall back to `defaultParameterEncoding` for a name with no encoding, and `body` is passed through. So, on `main`, a flow over a 3.x document with `$ref` path or query parameters dispatched those parameters and the call worked. The probe on this head's judge, using the shape the generator emits (`properties: { query: {...} }`, path params all `$ref`), returns `'path' is not an input the action declares (declared: 'query')` with the option on, and `undefined` without it. A `$ref` body gives `'body' is not an input the action declares (declared: 'path')`.
- **The Slack connector's schemas are partial (S2).** `chat.postMessage` and `chat.update` (slack-connector.ts ~101-131) list four parameters each and send the whole input to Slack (`callSlack('chat.postMessage', input)`). Any other Slack Web API parameter an author passes is now refused. The `call` action (`method` + `params`, where `params` is `type: 'object'` with no `properties`, so it is open) still carries one.
- **First-party claim.** Neither shipped OpenAPI document (`packages/apps/connector-docusign/openapi/…`, `packages/apps/connector-stripe/openapi/…`) has a `$ref` parameter or request body (counted on this tree). `connector-rest` `request` declares `headers`/`query` as objects with no `properties` (open) and `body` with no type. That is consistent with "First-party flows affected: 0". I did not re-read the first-party flows' inputs one by one.
- **CI on this head, read just before posting:** 70 check runs: 53 success, 13 skipped, none failed, and 4 still in progress (`Test Core` 1/8, 7/8 and 8/8, and `Test UI`). The successes include `TypeScript Type Check`, every `Type Check ·` and `Lint ·` job, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset` (both runs) and `Spec property liveness`. The PR is a draft.

### ② Semver level

- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is right, so the level is `minor`.** The refusal tightens a requirement on authored flow metadata: a key in `connectorConfig.input` that the action's schema admitted under JSON Schema's open default is now refused. The judge is the action's declared schema, which is connector metadata, not data state. That is the line that separates this PR from #27995 (`none`, `CHANGELOG.md` ~1716-1721), which refused only calls the declared schema itself already called wrong, and from the #33280 ruling (judged against database membership). `@objectstack/service-automation: minor` follows.
- **The ADR-0087 `registered` semantic entry is the right disposition.** No `migrate meta` conversion can choose between dropping a key and switching the action, so the judgment stays with the author. The entry's fields match `SemanticMigration` (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`). The Check Changeset log reads `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing+metadata-protocol-narrowed] registered connector-action-undeclared-input-key-refused (new here: …)` and `✓ LEVEL AXIS: … clause-② yes (narrowing) and metadata-protocol narrowed …`.
- **The arm is right, the value is not (S1).** `(narrowing)` is the right arm. `Clause-②: yes` declares that a published accept set or public surface widens (the gate's DECLARE block). Nothing widens here. `connector-input-schema.ts` is not re-exported from `src/index.ts`, and the package's `exports` has only `"."`. So `ConnectorInputJudgeOptions`, `UNDECLARED_KEY_HINT` and the new `undeclaredKey` field are internal. The spelling should be `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, as #27995 declared for the same door. #28040's `yes` was earned by a widened exported type. The gate does not decide the level from this value, so it stays green either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Same gap at the pull door.** The pull door (`connectorSource.input`) has the same gap and does not opt in. The PR names this as a sibling, not touched. It needs its own card.
- **No publish-time check.** A publish-time warning would need a sealed connector vocabulary, which does not exist. The PR names this too.
- **Draft.** The PR is a draft, authored by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- N1 (nit): the changeset says "at the top or inside a section". The walk also refuses an undeclared key inside an object in an array's `items`. Say "at every object level, array items included".
- N2 (nit): `KEY_ADMITTING_KEYWORDS` has `$dynamicRef` but not the 2019-09 `$recursiveRef`. An MCP tool schema of that draft would be read as closed.
- N3 (nit): the PR adds a file to `@objectstack/spec` but carries no spec line in a changeset. The `fixed` group moves spec's version with service-automation's, so the entry ships. The recent semantic-entry PRs (#33442 `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, #33513 a separate spec `patch` changeset) each named spec.
- N4 (nit): the "pull door unchanged" pin calls `judgeConnectorInput` without the option. It does not run `pullConnectorSource`. The door's source is untouched, so this holds today.

### ④ Design judgment

- **(1) A run-time-only refusal is acceptable.** #33553's acceptance allows "refused loudly (at publish, or at run)". A registration-time verdict would be read before declarative connectors materialize (verified in ①). That is the defect AGENTS.md "Startup registry reads — never record a verdict the boot can still contradict" names. Reading the schema of the instance the call dispatches to is the only verdict the boot cannot contradict.
- **(2) The rule "declared = `properties` ∪ `required`, open if it admits more" is sound as a reading of a schema.** Its open set is complete for the keywords that can carry keys (save N2). Reading `properties` as the contract is what closes #33553. But the rule assumes every producer lists every input the action takes, and two producers do not. connector-openapi drops `$ref` parameters and `$ref` or schemaless bodies (M1). Slack's two message actions list a subset of what they forward (S2).
- **M1 (must-fix): the migration does not cover the non-normalized OpenAPI class.** For a declarative `openapi` connector over a 3.x document with `$ref` parameters or a `$ref`/schemaless request body, a call that dispatches and works on `main` is now refused. The prescribed fix, "drop the key, or pick the action that declares it", cannot be followed: the parameter is needed, and no action declares it. AGENTS.md requires a breaking changeset to carry its migration, and the semantic entry's `replacement` ships in spec as the prescription. Either change closes M1:
  - (a) Preferred: `buildInputSchema` marks what it skipped as open. A location with a skipped `$ref` parameter gets `additionalProperties: true` on that section, and the section is emitted even when every parameter in it was a `$ref`. A `$ref` or schemaless body gets `body: {}`. Add a pin that a `$ref`-parameter document still dispatches. This needs connector-openapi in the lane's file surface.
  - (b) The changeset's BREAKING/migration text and the semantic entry's `replacement` name this class and its fix: normalize the document with `normalize-openapi` so the action declares the parameter.
- **S2 (should-fix).** The BREAKING text should name the partial pass-through case: Slack `chat.postMessage`/`chat.update` now refuse a Slack parameter the schema does not list, and the fix is the `call` action with `params`.
- **S1 (should-fix).** Change `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` to `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset.
- **Otherwise the design holds.** The judgment is opt-in on the shared helper. The refusal is the same routable `VALIDATION_ERROR`, judged on the evaluated input, and it names the declared keys at the failing level. `undefined` counts as absent and `null` is refused. These match the #27995 contract this extends, and the tests pin each one.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-A5-33553`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cxDxAYxdtDhtR1kQQe`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
M1 must change: either the OpenAPI generator declares what it skips as open (preferred), or the changeset and the semantic entry prescribe normalizing the document. S1 and S2 should be fixed in the same pass. N1 to N4 are nits.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `188a8286353413c982a115f6f5831e08322bb9ff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-action-undeclared-input-key-refused.ts + .changeset/33553-connector-action-undeclared-input-key.md, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/input-schema-dispatch.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-input-schema.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-input-schema.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts; read only: packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-slack/src/slack-connector.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/apps/connector-stripe/openapi/stripe.openapi.json, packages/apps/connector-docusign/openapi/docusign-esignature.openapi.json, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/connector-input-fields.ts, skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A5 · Fixes #33553 (p2) · delta review after the FAIL record 6888662219 at `10a4106a18`. Read only: `git diff 10a4106a..188a8286` on a fetched ref, the current PR body, the changeset, the cited producers at this head, and this head's check runs, including the Check Changeset job log. Nothing built or run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

- **What moved since `10a4106a18`.** Three commits. `d4822373` changes the connector-openapi generator and adds a pin. `753c427e` edits the changeset, the semantic entry, `KEY_ADMITTING_KEYWORDS`, one test title, and adds a pull-door pin. `188a8286` merges `origin/main`. That merge changes none of the PR's 8 files, and nothing under `packages/connectors/`, `connector-nodes.ts`, `connector-input-schema.ts` or `connector-pull.ts` (`git diff --stat 753c427e 188a8286` on those paths is empty).
- **M1 is resolved by option (a).** In `buildInputSchema` (openapi-connector.ts ~524-575), a `$ref` parameter sets `unresolvedParameter`. Then `path`, `query` and `header` are each emitted with `additionalProperties: true`, including a location that declares no parameter of its own. `declaredKeysOf` reads that as open. `path` is required only when it declares a parameter. Any object `requestBody` is now declared as `extractRequestBodySchema(...) ?? {}`. So a `$ref` body, or content with no `schema`, becomes `body: {}`, which is open and has no type. `required` gains `body` only for an inline required body. The declarative `openapi` provider builds through the same `createOpenApiConnector` (openapi-provider.ts ~275), so it emits the same schema. The parameters declared next to a `$ref` are still judged.
- **The M1 pin runs end to end.** The new describe in `input-schema-dispatch.test.ts` boots a `LiteKernel` with the engine and `ConnectorOpenApiPlugin` over a 3.0.3 document. That document has a `$ref` path parameter, a `$ref` query parameter, a declared `limit`, a `$ref` request body, and an `application/octet-stream` body with no schema. Each case dispatches through a `connector_action` flow with `fetch` recorded. Case 1 asserts the emitted section shapes and `required` undefined. It then sends `{ path: { petId: 7 }, query: { tag, limit }, body }` and checks the URL is `/pets/7?…tag=dog`, with the JSON body sent. It also checks that `limit: 'two'` is still refused and nothing more is sent. Case 2 asserts `body: {}`, `required: ['path', 'body']` and a closed `path`, and checks the raw body dispatches. I checked each assertion against the code above. The run itself is CI's (see the last bullet).
- **Nothing else is newly refused in generated actions.** Compared with `10a4106a18`, each change opens something: it adds `additionalProperties: true`, drops `path` from `required` when it declares nothing, or adds `body: {}`. One shape is judged that was not judged before. An operation whose only inputs were `$ref` parameters, or a `$ref`/schemaless body, used to get no `inputSchema` (`buildInputSchema` returned `undefined`). It now gets one, so a top-level key outside the emitted sections is refused. The document declares no such input, so this is the declared narrowing applied the same way it already applies to an operation with a typed body. It is not the M1 shape. The other generator skips are unchanged at this head: `cookie`, the OAS-ignored `Accept`/`Content-Type`/`Authorization`, the auth's own header or query parameter, and scheme-filled parameters (see N6).
- **S2 is resolved.** The changeset adds a paragraph naming the partial pass-through case: `chat.postMessage`/`chat.update` list four keys each and forward the whole input. It names the refused examples and gives a FROM → TO to `call` with `method` + `params`. At this head `params` is `{ type: 'object' }` with no `properties` (slack-connector.ts ~133-142), so it is open. The semantic entry's `replacement` names the same fix.
- **S1 is resolved in the changeset only.** The changeset now reads `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The PR body line 6 still reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. That is the line the gate reads. This head's Check Changeset log prints ``✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `yes (narrowing)` …`` and ``· declaration line: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — …` ``. The PR body has not been refreshed for this head either. It cites `head f1f1ace963`, does not mention the connector-openapi change, the Slack paragraph or `$recursiveRef`, and has no `Skills-docs:` line.
- **The nits are taken.** N1: the changeset, the semantic entry `surface` and the test doc all say "at every object level, array items included". N2: `$recursiveRef` is in `KEY_ADMITTING_KEYWORDS`, with a pin for both it and `$dynamicRef`. N3: the changeset names `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. N4: `connector-pull.test.ts` now runs `pullConnectorSource` with an undeclared top-level key and an undeclared `query` key, and asserts the handler received both unchanged. The old judge-level case is renamed to what it pins.
- **CI on this head, read just before posting:** 67 check runs: 56 success, 11 skipped, none failed or pending. The successes include every required context that ran (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`; `Lint UI` was skipped), plus `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness`. The Test Core shard logs show `src/input-schema-dispatch.test.ts (6 tests)` passing, with connector-openapi at `Tests 111 passed (111)` (the PR body's earlier count was 109). They also show `src/builtin/connector-input-schema.test.ts (23 tests)` and `src/connector-pull.test.ts (53 tests)` passing. The PR is a draft.

### ② Semver level

- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed` still stands, so each moved package is `minor`.** The level is unchanged from the first record. The connector-openapi change only widens what the refusal admits, so the kind does not change. The changeset now moves three packages: `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/connector-openapi` and `@objectstack/spec`, each `minor`. That matches "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves". Check Changeset is green and reads the level axis as satisfied.
- **The ADR-0087 `registered` disposition still holds.** The log reads `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing+metadata-protocol-narrowed] registered connector-action-undeclared-input-key-refused`. The entry keeps its `SemanticMigration` fields. Only the `surface` and `replacement` prose changed, and neither carries a tracker number.
- **The Clause-② value is still `yes` where the gate reads it (S1, open).** The changeset is right. The PR body is not. As before, the gate does not grade the level from this value, so CI stays green either way. The declaration is still wrong on the surface the gate reads.
